Parley is an open-source chat app for communities: servers, channels, DMs, voice, video, stages and a recording studio. Start free right now on app.runparley.com, or run it on your own server and keep every byte.
Parley desktop app: a voice channel called Jam Room with four people, one speaking, one sharing a screen, and the call control bar.
Jump in on our server today. If your community wants its own, move to a server you run whenever you're ready.
Free, with nothing to install or configure. Make an account, start a server for your group, and send the invite link.
Start a server, or join one from an invite
Two Docker images and Postgres on your PC, Raspberry Pi, NAS or VPS. Your data stays on your hardware, and you decide who gets in.

Discord puts its best features behind a $9.99 monthly subscription and sells your profile back to you in a shop. On Parley everyone gets the top tier, the code is open for anyone to read, and your community can move to a server you own whenever you like.

No Nitro, no boosts, no shop. Hi-fi voice, 60 fps streams, profile flair and the bigger limits come with a free account. Parley isn't holding anything back to sell you later.
Start on app.runparley.com, then move to your own PC, NAS or VPS with one Docker command. There, nobody else can delete your community, change the rules on you or shut the app down.

Age checks use a birth date, not a scan of your passport. In 2025 ID photos people had sent for Discord's age checks leaked from one of its support vendors. Parley never asks for them, and there are no ad trackers or sponsored posts.
The whole app is open source: audit it, fork it, change it. End-to-end encrypted calls, an MCP connector for your AI assistant and a recording studio are built in, not bolted on.

The whole hangout, not just the chat.
Text when you want to read, voice when you want to talk, a stage when you want an audience. All of it lives on one server you control.

Threads, forum channels, polls, pins, bookmarks, replies and full markdown. Write a message now and schedule it for later: it goes out on time even with your device off, and you can send it early, edit or cancel it from your Inbox. Mentions badge the server they happened in, "Seen" shows when your DM was read, and coming back to a channel tells you how many messages are new and marks where you left off.
@Mara the bridge on take 3 is the one. Bouncing stems now.
Two to ten answers, single or multiple choice, and a timer from an hour to a week. Results update live for everyone.
Drop in, talk, share your screen

Peer-to-peer calls that suit rooms of about six to eight. For bigger rooms, point Parley at a LiveKit server. Screen shares start when you click Watch Stream, so nobody downloads a stream they aren't looking at. Turn on end-to-end encryption for a channel or a DM and only the people in the call can see and hear it, not even the server, with a safety code you can compare out loud. Push-to-talk, noise suppression and per-device settings apply live.
Speakers on stage, everyone else listening. Raise a hand to ask to speak; moderators invite you up. Schedule events with RSVPs and a reminder ten minutes before.
Record a clip from the message box. With transcription switched on, a local Whisper server writes out what was said.
"Okay, I re-amped the guitar, check the stems channel."
Roles, permissions and the tools to run the place

Moving from Discord? Import a server template and your categories, channels, roles and permissions come with you. Coloured and gradient roles with a real hierarchy, per-channel overrides, private channels, timeouts, bans, member screening and an audit log. Custom emoji and stickers per server. Invite links that expire when you choose, from 30 minutes to never, with an optional use limit. List your server in Discover when you want new people to find it, and claim up to three vanity links like /invite/your-name. Put a live badge on your README or site, like the one at the top of this page: it shows who's online and opens your invite.
Sign in with a passkey or a password plus two-factor codes. A device list you can log out remotely, rate limits, reports, and optional ClamAV scanning of every upload before it is stored.

Audio files get a proper player with a live visualiser (bars, a wave or a pulsing orb, in your theme's colour), seeking, speed and volume. Playback follows you around: switch channels and a now-playing bar keeps the controls, even on a locked phone. Tracks count their listens the way streaming services do, videos open full screen instead of in a tiny box, and on phones you can save or share any file in a tap.
An app that keeps itself current

The Windows, macOS and Linux apps draw their own title bar with back and forward, where you are and your inbox. New versions download in the background and a green arrow restarts you into them. Want the newest changes first? Switch the update channel to Development.

A full web app plus Windows, macOS, Linux and Android apps that open app.runparley.com in one tap or connect to any Parley server you choose. Phones get a one-pane layout, and the interface speaks 14 languages.
Nightly backups with a restore script, Prometheus metrics, JSON logs, Sentry errors, a mail log in the admin console, and more than one backend behind a load balancer when you grow.

Profile frames, animated effects, nameplates, avatar decorations, styled names, server tags, banners and profile panels, all from one editor with a live preview. Hosting your own? Make decorations, nameplates, effects and frames in the admin console from a picture, two colours or an emoji, or drop them into a folder, and everyone on your server can pick them straight away.
Keep a personal and a work account signed in side by side and hop between them from your profile menu. No password prompts, no logging out.

Parley speaks MCP, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other assistants can catch you up on unreads and mentions, search, reply and react. Add your server's /mcp address as a connector, sign in, and tick what it may do. Server management stays off unless you allow it, and you can disconnect it any time.
Jonah posted new stems and asked you to check the vocal bus. Rae mentioned you about Friday's session. Want me to reply?
Frames that hang off your card, effects that play when someone opens your profile, nameplates behind your name, and one editor with a live preview for all of it.

A profile card for Mara with a gradient frame, a star on top, sparkles drifting over it, a styled name with a server tag, Add Friend and Message buttons, roles, and an In voice card with a Join Voice button.

Frames reach past the edge of your card and effects play their full animation over it. Hover any effect in the picker to watch it first. Hosting your own server? Drop decorations, nameplates, effects and frames into your assets folder with a metadata.json, no restart needed.
Avatar, decoration, banner, theme, name style, nameplate, effect, frame, tags and badges, with your card updating as you go. Nothing changes until you hit Save.

Open someone in a server and you see their roles there and when they joined, and if they're in voice, a Join Voice button. The full profile adds their activity, mutual friends and servers, wishlist, games and reviews.
Servers design a tag with a badge and a colour, and members wear it next to their name. Click anyone's tag to see the server behind it and apply to join.
Jam live. Leave with the multitrack.
A studio is a voice channel built for music, with a console for the engineer. Everyone in the band records their own track in full quality, so a bad connection never ruins a take.
The engineer's console recording Take 3 at 120 BPM in 4/4 with the metronome on: three armed tracks, keys, vocals and bass, each with a level meter, and the bass punched in partway through the take.
The engineer gets a small DAW: lanes on a timeline that grow as the band plays, and a mixer with a strip per artist for pan, fader, mute, solo and arm. Tab switches views, like Ableton Live.
Record who you need, when you need
Arm only the players a take needs. Arm someone mid-take and they punch in on the spot; disarm them and they punch out. Late arrivals to the band join the take automatically.
Set the tempo and time signature, turn on the click and add a count-in of one to four bars. Each player hears it in their own ears, in time with the take, and it never ends up in the recording.
Engineers start and stop takes. Artists are heard and recorded. Everyone else listens from the audience until an engineer brings them in.
Music doesn't get treated like speech
High-fidelity channels switch off noise suppression and echo cancellation, send stereo Opus at up to 510 kbps, and can drop to 10 ms frames for tighter timing.
Every take opens with waveforms lined up automatically, live meters, per-track gain, pan, mute and solo, and a master fader. Export renders a 48 kHz, 16-bit WAV of the mix.
Parley ships as two Docker images and a Postgres database. If your machine runs Docker, it runs Parley: a spare PC, a Raspberry Pi, a NAS or a VPS.
